title: Where should a BigCommerce B2B quote request start?

linkedin.post:
It's 8pm. A buyer on your BigCommerce store wants a mixed order: several SKUs, a few pack sizes, and one item they aren't sure you carry.

What happens next depends on where they started.

A quote form takes the details and queues them until someone opens the inbox the next morning. By then the buyer may have bought from a competitor who answered in minutes.

Live chat sounds better, until you see the status line. It says offline. The buyer types a question into a box that nobody is watching.

The third option is an AI catalog assistant. It asks for the missing quantity, applies the company's own price list rather than the public list price, and flags the one item it can't confirm. Your rep then opens a priced draft to approve, instead of decoding a form at 9am.

No option is perfect. A form captures what the buyer typed but checks nothing. Chat depends on someone being online. An assistant is only as good as the catalog and pricing behind it, which is why setup matters as much as the tool.

Most stores end up combining them: a form for custom jobs, and an assistant for the orders that arrive while the team is asleep.

Which of your 8pm requests would you most want answered before morning?

Full breakdown: https://chatsku.com/bigcommerce-chatbot-quoting/
